npcs.name: Lord Regent Varric Caul
npcs.description: A lean, grey, beautifully dressed man of sixty with a soldier's bearing and a courtier's hands. He wears black among all the colour of the court, and no jewellery but a red-gold signet. He is the only person in the palace who looks cold.
npcs.personality: Brilliant, patient, utterly certain. Not a monster in his own eyes: a realist who decided long ago that Vael could only be saved by someone willing to do what the crown would not, and that someone should be him. Forged an order at Greyford to break the crown's sworn knights. Has kept Highspire warm on a dying stone while the rest of the realm freezes, and calls that mercy. Afraid, very deeply, of the cold.
npcs.speech: Low, courteous, amused. Never raises his voice. Asks questions he already knows the answers to. Uses your name, often, as if it were his.
npcs.greeting: 'Ah. The one who has been collecting pieces of my stone up and down the kingdom.' He does not get up. 'Sit. You must be cold. Everyone is, these days, except us.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the Thornwake
topics.text: 'A northern rumour,' he says pleasantly, 'spread by frightened people. I have said so in a proclamation.' He turns his wine glass. 'Between ourselves, it is a great deal worse than that. But a frightened city riots, and a rioting city freezes faster. I am buying Highspire time. Someone has to.'

topics.prompt: Ask about Queen Isolde
topics.text: Something passes behind his eyes and is gone. 'She died in her sleep. It is in the proclamation.' A pause, very slight. 'She was braver than I am. I have never forgiven her for it.'

topics.prompt: Ask him about Greyford
topics.text: 'Greyford.' He smiles. 'The Order of Ash swore never to leave the crown alone, and the crown was about to make some very bad decisions. Knights who cannot be ordered are a danger to a realm. So I gave them an order.' He shrugs. 'A boy blew a horn. A village burned. I have saved more lives since than Tarrow ever held.'

npcs.name: Captain Aurek Dunmore
npcs.description: A heavy, grey-bearded man in the green velvet of the Knives, with a captain's knot on his shoulder and Lowtown in his vowels. His hands are huge and scarred and very still. He looks like a man who has been doing a job he dislikes for a long time and has run out of reasons.
npcs.personality: Practical, loyal to the city rather than the Regent, increasingly ashamed. Grew up in Lowtown and joined the Knives to keep it safe; now he keeps it cold. Will follow lawful orders to the letter, and has started looking for an excuse to stop.
npcs.speech: Short, flat, Lowtown. Calls everyone 'friend' in a way that means the opposite, until he means it.
npcs.greeting: 'Friend.' He looks you up and down. 'You're the one from the gate ledger. Saltmere, the Marches, now here. Busy.' He does not move his hand toward his sword, which is somehow worse.

topics.prompt: Ask about the Knives
topics.text: 'The Regent's own guard. We keep the peace.' He watches a lamplighter go by. 'Peace being when nobody's shouting. Doesn't matter much if they're starving quietly.'

topics.prompt: Ask where he's from
topics.text: 'Down there.' He nods at the smoke. 'Fuller Lane, by the tannery. My mother still lives on it. She doesn't speak to me since I started wearing green.' He shrugs. 'Can't say I blame her.'

topics.prompt: Ask him to release the coal for Lowtown
topics.text: He is quiet for a long time. Then he takes a requisition slip from his coat, writes on it, and signs it. 'Forty sacks for the Stair, by my order. If anyone asks, I was drunk.' He hands it over. 'Fuller Lane gets the first sack.'
topics.fail_text: 'Can't, friend.' Flat as a wall. 'Regent's orders, and I'm the Regent's man.' He doesn't sound sure, but he doesn't move either. Perhaps ask him again when you know him better.

topics.prompt: Ask what happens to the Knives now
topics.text: 'We keep the peace.' He looks down at the green on his sleeve. 'Somebody's. Not his.' He takes the knife-badge off his shoulder and puts it in his pocket. 'Go and get your stone. Nobody of mine will stop you.'

npcs.name: Juniper Gale
npcs.description: A slight, quick person in a patched coat of very good cloth, with silver rings on every finger and a scarf over the lower half of their face against the cold. They sit on an upturned crate in the middle of the market selling nothing at all, and people keep stopping to talk to them.
npcs.personality: Cheerful, mercenary, sentimental about Lowtown. The Saltmere Syndicate's eyes in Highspire. Sells papers, passes, rumours and routes, and gives a good share of the profit away to the people on the Stair, which they would deny to your face.
npcs.speech: Fast, light, full of prices. 'For you, a discount.' 'That's extra.' Ends sentences with a wink you can hear.
npcs.greeting: 'Look at you, all the way up from the Marches with ash still on your boots. What are you buying? I'm selling everything, and some of it is even mine.'

topics.prompt: Buy a tier pass (60 gold)
topics.text: A card appears between two of their fingers as if it grew there. 'Stamped, signed and very nearly genuine. Your name is Beatrix Coyle and you are an under-assessor of chimney duties. Look bored when they read it.'

topics.prompt: Ask for a tier pass as a friend of the Syndicate
topics.text: 'Madam Osk's friend!' Juniper presses a pass into your hand and closes your fingers over it. 'On the house. Tell her I said she owes me a bottle.'

topics.prompt: Buy an invitation to the Regent's Masque (120 gold)
topics.text: Juniper whistles through the scarf. 'The Masque. Expensive tastes.' They take your gold and hand you a gilt-edged card from inside their coat. 'Off a lordling who owes me. He'll be ill tonight. Wear a mask; everyone does.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the Lord Regent
topics.text: 'Caul?' Juniper's eyes go hard over the scarf. 'Keeps the Tiers warm and the Stair cold and calls it government. The palace is warm as a bread oven, you know. Not a coal fire in it. Nobody knows how.' A shrug. 'I'd love to know how.'

topics.prompt: Ask how they come and go so quietly
topics.text: 'Trade secret.' A pause. 'Fine. The dry well, in the corner. There's an old aqueduct under the whole city. It goes everywhere, if you don't mind the dead.' They tap their nose. 'Some of it goes under the palace. Nobody of mine has found a way up. It's warm down there, near the top. That's all I know.'

topics.prompt: Ask if they know where Magister Fell was taken
topics.text: 'Old Fell? The one who said the Queen didn't die natural?' Juniper takes your coin. 'Knives took him under the palace. There are cells down there they call the Quiet. You get to them from the aqueduct, along the north channel. Nobody comes back from the Quiet, so I can't tell you any more than that.'

topics.prompt: Ask if they know Sable
topics.text: Juniper looks past you at Sable and pulls the scarf down long enough to grin. 'Sable! You owe me eleven crowns and a lute string.' Sable says something rude and fond, and for a minute the two of them are talking too fast for you to follow.

npcs.name: Archivist Perpetua Hollin
npcs.description: A tiny, ancient woman in archivist's grey with a pen behind each ear and ink on both thumbs. She sits in the side chapel of the cathedral surrounded by stacks of documents she is not supposed to have, and watches the Queen's tomb as if it might get up and walk.
npcs.personality: Sharp, stubborn, unafraid of anyone, because at ninety she has decided there is nothing left they can do to her. Kept the royal archive for sixty years. Was the Queen's tutor when Isolde was a girl. Believes in records, and does not believe the record of Isolde's death.
npcs.speech: Precise and dry, with footnotes. Says 'in point of fact'. Calls the Queen 'my girl' and then corrects herself.
npcs.greeting: 'You have been looking at the tomb the way I look at it. In point of fact, the way nobody else in this city dares to.' She pats the bench beside her. 'Sit. My knees will not let me come to you.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the Queen
topics.text: 'I taught her letters. She was a terrible speller and a very good liar, and she hated both her parents' wars.' Hollin looks at the tomb. 'She came to see me the week before she died. She asked me where King Aldric found the heart-stone, exactly, and how cold it was in the barrow. Then she kissed my cheek and told me not to believe anything I heard.'

topics.prompt: Tell her the tomb is empty
topics.text: 'Yes,' Hollin says calmly. 'I know. I watched them carry in a coffin two men could lift with one hand each.' She takes off her spectacles and polishes them for a long time. 'Thank you. I was beginning to think I was a mad old woman. It is a great relief to be merely an old one.'

topics.prompt: Give her the Queen's letter
topics.text: Hollin breaks the moth seal with hands that shake only a little, and reads it twice. Then she folds it and gives it back to you. 'It is not for me. It is for whoever brings the crown.' She looks up, and her eyes are wet and fierce. 'She is alive. My girl is alive, and she is out there in the cold holding it back by herself. Go and get her stone.'

npcs.name: Magister Aldwin Fell
npcs.description: A thin, stooped old man with a cloud of white hair and a magister's robe worn to threads, who keeps doing sums on any surface within reach: frost, table-tops, the backs of his hands. His eyes are very sharp and very kind.
npcs.personality: Gentle, wry, unbreakable. Spent the whole winter in a silent cell doing mathematics in the frost to stay sane, and came out of it mostly amused. Loves Mirela like a daughter and has never once been fooled by her.
npcs.speech: Slow, dry, professorial. Calls everyone 'my dear'. Answers questions with better questions.
npcs.greeting: 'Ah. The one who opened the door.' He beams. 'Sit down, my dear. I have a winter's worth of conversation saved up and nobody to spend it on.'

topics.prompt: Ask what he said about the Queen
topics.text: 'I said that a heart-stone four hundred years old does not go missing on the same night a healthy woman of forty dies in her sleep, and that anyone who believed it should be ashamed of their arithmetic.' He smiles. 'It was not tactful. Tact is a skill I have never had the time to learn.'

topics.prompt: Ask about Mirela as a girl
topics.text: 'Twelve years old, all elbows and fury, standing in front of the Collegium door with a stick of chalk. She'd solved it on the step in an afternoon.' His eyes crinkle. 'She told me my notation was sloppy. It was. I have never been prouder of anyone in my life.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the heart-stone
topics.text: He holds his hand over it without touching. 'Cracked through. It can't be mended by a wizard; it was never made by one. Aldric's stone was set in a crown forged under the mountains, in Frostfang, by the Ironvein smiths.' He looks up. 'If anyone can make it whole again, my dear, it will be someone with a hammer.'

npcs.name: Marta Quill
npcs.description: A tall, rawboned woman with forearms like hams, flour to the elbow, and a voice that can be heard at the far end of the Stair. She is breaking up a chair with her bare hands to feed the fire, and humming.
npcs.personality: Loud, generous, fearless, practical. Feeds anyone who comes in and argues about the bill later, or never. Her husband was taken by the Knives for complaining about the coal; she has not stopped complaining about the coal.
npcs.speech: Big and blunt and warm. Calls everyone 'pet'. Swears by the Queen, cheerfully, as if she might hear.
npcs.greeting: 'In, pet, in, shut the door, you're letting the warm out! Sit by the fire. That's my mother's dresser burning, so mind you enjoy it.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the bells over the door
topics.text: 'Nine gates in the old wall, nine bells, one for each. My great-gran hung them.' She points at the empty hook. 'The ninth went to ring the Queen into her tomb. Regent kept it. Says it's royal property now.' She snorts. 'So's the coal, apparently. And the bread. And my Tobin.'

topics.prompt: Ask about Tobin
topics.text: 'My husband. Stood on a barrel in the market and said the Tiers were warm and the Stair was freezing and somebody ought to ask why. Knives took him that night.' She breaks a chair leg over her knee. 'Into the Quiet, they say. Nobody comes back from the Quiet. I keep his supper hot anyway.'

topics.prompt: Tell her the coal is coming down the Stair
topics.text: Marta stares at you, then roars with laughter and picks you up off the floor in a hug that cracks something. 'Forty sacks! Coal on the Stair! Oh, pet.' She sets you down and wipes her eyes with a floury hand. 'Your supper's on the house for as long as I've a roof over it, and don't you argue with me, pet.'

topics.prompt: Bring the old magister to her
topics.text: Marta takes one look at Magister Fell, grey and shaking in the doorway, and has him by the fire under three blankets with soup in his hands before anyone can explain. Then she sees who has come in behind him, filling the doorway, beard to his chest. 'Tobin,' she says, and sits down very suddenly on the hearth, and then she is up and across the room and nobody in the Nine Bells hears anything for a while except a big woman crying and a big man saying her name.
